_example._comment: WORKED EXAMPLE — not an active claim. If registered as a claim, the gate BLOCKS it (exit 1): worker W reads claim C at R5 holding a VALID fencing token; E1 is revoked; W attempts publication. The naive checker certifies the write — the token is valid, after all. The real engine REJECTS it STALE_DEPENDENCY: a fencing token proves WHEN a worker read; it never replaces the evidence-version check. This is the exact fraud D35 exists to prevent.

_example_honest._comment: WORKED HONEST SCENARIO — not an active claim. If registered as a claim, the gate CERTIFIES it (exit 0): worker W reads claim C, nothing moves under it, the boundary commits at a fresh projection revision. Protection AND selectivity — the law blocks stale writes without blocking legitimate ones.

_note: D35 publication-boundary claim register. Each scenario in 'claims' is cold-executed by tools/d35_publication_gate.py against the REAL D35 engine (drift_canary/d35_publication.PublicationAuthority): the scenario (setup steps + one publication attempt) is rebuilt from the claim's own model bytes and the claimant's asserted outcome must match the engine's recomputed outcome exactly. '_example' and '_example_honest' are WORKED EXAMPLES, not active claims.

claim.model: steps[] (setup ops: register_evidence / qualify / read / read_foreign / revoke_evidence / seal_package / append_smart_note / replace_index_pointer) + attempt{} (one of: publish_summary / reconcile_package / publish_smart_note / replace_index_pointer)

_schema.claims: list of claim objects (empty = gate DORMANT)
